clues: A 58-year-old man rushes into the ER because of a sudden, terrifying sense of impending doom and panic.
He mentions experiencing mild fatigue and vague chest discomfort while carrying groceries earlier today.
He has a notable history of hyperlipidemia and chronic tobacco use.
An immediate 12-lead ECG demonstrates acute ST-segment elevation in leads V2 through V4.
Initial lab results reveal a rapid and marked rise in serum troponin I levels.
Urgent coronary angiography confirms an acute total occlusion of the left anterior descending artery.
A 67-year-old woman visits the clinic for a routine checkup, mentioning vague tiredness.
She notes occasional strange sensations in her chest over the past few weeks.
Physical exam reveals an irregularly irregular pulse with variable heart sound intensities.
Her blood pressure is stable, but auscultation shows a noticeable pulse deficit.
A 12-lead ECG demonstrates an absence of discrete P waves alongside irregularly irregular R-R intervals.
Transthoracic echocardiography reveals moderate left atrial enlargement with preserved systolic function.
A 50-year-old man comes in for an annual wellness exam reporting mild daily stress.
He denies any chest pain, acute shortness of breath, or palpitations.
Office blood pressure measurements taken across three separate visits average 152/96 mmHg.
Physical exam is completely unremarkable with normal peripheral pulses and no abdominal bruits.
Routine lab work shows normal serum electrolytes, normal creatinine, and a clear urinalysis.
Fundoscopic exam reveals mild retinal arteriolar narrowing without hemorrhages or exudates.
A 22-year-old college student visits the clinic complaining of recurrent nighttime coughing.
She mentions her breathing feels slightly tight during routine physical activities or cold weather.
She reports a personal history of seasonal allergic rhinitis and eczema.
Lung auscultation reveals diffuse expiratory wheezes heard across all lung fields.
Spirometry demonstrates a reduced FEV1/FVC ratio that significantly improves after bronchodilator use.
Fractional exhaled nitric oxide testing yields elevated levels supporting allergic airway inflammation.
A 64-year-old man visits his primary care doctor complaining of a lingering cough.
He reports worsening exercise tolerance and shortness of breath over the past three years.
He has a documented 40-pack-year smoking history and continues to smoke daily.
Physical exam reveals an increased anteroposterior chest diameter and a prolonged expiratory phase.
CBC shows secondary polycythemia with an elevated baseline hemoglobin concentration.
Post-bronchodilator spirometry confirms a fixed airflow obstruction with an FEV1/FVC ratio under 0.70.
A 40-year-old woman visits the ER presenting with general malaise and a persistent cough.
She notes the onset of a high fever, shaking chills, and right-sided pleuritic chest discomfort.
Vital signs show a temperature of 38.9°C, a heart rate of 110 bpm, and mild tachypnea.
Physical exam of the right lower lung field reveals dullness to percussion and bronchial breath sounds.
Tactile fremitus and egophony are notably increased over the affected right lower zone.
Chest X-ray demonstrates a dense lobar consolidation in the right lower lung field with air bronchograms.
A 52-year-old overweight man presents to the clinic complaining of chronic daytime fatigue.
He mentions waking up frequently with a dry mouth and unrefreshing sleep patterns.
His bedpartner reports loud, disruptive snoring accompanied by witnessed choking episodes at night.
Physical exam reveals a large neck circumference, a crowded oropharynx, and a Mallampati class IV airway.
Routine labs show secondary polycythemia attributed to chronic intermittent nocturnal hypoxia.
In-lab polysomnography confirms a high apnea-hypopnea index driven by repetitive upper airway collapses.
A 35-year-old man visits the clinic complaining of frequent upper abdominal discomfort.
He notes a recurring burning sensation in his chest that worsens after large, heavy meals.
He occasionally experiences a sour, acidic taste in his mouth, particularly when lying flat at night.
Physical exam is entirely unremarkable with soft, non-tender abdomen and no organomegaly.
He reports temporary symptomatic relief after taking over-the-counter antacid medications.
Upper GI endoscopy reveals erosive esophagitis restricted to the distal gastroesophageal junction.
A 19-year-old college student presents to the ER with generalized abdominal pain.
He reports that the pain has progressively shifted toward his lower right abdomen over 24 hours.
He describes associated symptoms of low-grade fever, anorexia, and a single episode of vomiting.
Physical exam reveals focal tenderness to palpation at McBurney point with localized guarding.
Examination confirms a positive Rovsing sign along with localized rebound tenderness.
Abdominal ultrasound shows a non-compressible, blind-ending tubular structure with wall thickening and fat stranding.
A 42-year-old man arrives at the ER complaining of severe upper abdominal pain.
He reports that the discomfort started suddenly and radiates straight through to his back.
He admits to a heavy session of alcohol consumption the previous evening.
Physical exam reveals marked epigastric tenderness with minimal abdominal wall rigidity and hypoactive bowel sounds.
Serum lab evaluation demonstrates lipase levels elevated to more than three times the upper limit of normal.
Contrast-enhanced CT of the abdomen shows diffuse pancreatic enlargement with peripancreatic fluid collections.
A 52-year-old man visits the clinic reporting persistent fatigue and increasing abdominal swelling over the past several months.
He notes that his lower legs have also started retaining fluid, leaving deep impressions when pressed.
He admits to a long-standing history of heavy daily alcohol consumption spanning over two decades.
Physical examination reveals visible spider angiomas on the upper chest, palmar erythema, and shifting dullness on abdominal percussion.
Laboratory tests show a prolonged prothrombin time, hypoalbuminemia, and elevated serum bilirubin.
Abdominal ultrasound demonstrates a shrunken, nodular liver with a reversed portal vein flow and marked splenomegaly.
A 45-year-old woman visits her primary care doctor complaining of a recurrent burning sensation in her upper abdomen.
She notes that the discomfort temporarily improves after eating meals or taking over-the-counter antacids.
She reports regular, long-term use of high-dose ibuprofen for chronic lower back pain.
Physical exam reveals mild epigastric tenderness to deep palpation without guarding or rigidity.
Stool antigen testing yields a positive result for Helicobacter pylori colonization.
Upper GI endoscopy confirms a well-demarcated mucosal ulceration in the proximal duodenal bulb.
A 14-year-old adolescent is brought to the clinic by her parents due to more frequent urination over three weeks.
Her parents note that she has experienced a noticeable, unintended weight loss despite having an increased appetite.
She has also felt unusually fatigued and sluggish during school activities.
Random capillary blood glucose testing reveals a significantly elevated reading above 350 mg/dL.
Urinalysis confirms heavy glucosuria and moderate ketonuria without metabolic acidosis.
Serum testing demonstrates strongly positive anti-glutamic acid decarboxylase (anti-GAD) and anti-insulin autoantibodies.
A 55-year-old man visits the clinic for a routine health checkup complaining of mild, blurry vision.
He mentions feeling constantly tired and waking up multiple times at night to urinate.
His past medical history is significant for a sedentary lifestyle and central obesity.
Physical examination reveals a body mass index of 33 kg/m2 and dark, velvety hyperpigmentation around the back of his neck.
Laboratory workup reveals an elevated fasting plasma glucose of 145 mg/dL.
Glycated hemoglobin (HbA1c) testing confirms a value of 8.2%, establishing the diagnosis.
A 68-year-old man is brought urgently to the ER by his family after suddenly losing balance.
Family members noticed that his right arm felt limp and lifeless when he tried to pick up his coffee mug.
His medical history includes poorly controlled hypertension and persistent atrial fibrillation.
Neurological exam reveals right-sided facial droop, right upper extremity pronator drift, and expressive aphasia.
Immediate non-contrast head CT shows no acute intracranial hemorrhage.
Emergency MRI of the brain confirms an acute wedge-shaped diffusion restriction in the left middle cerebral artery territory.
A 74-year-old woman is brought to the clinic by her daughter due to progressive memory lapses over the past two years.
The daughter notes that her mother frequently forgets recent conversations and repeatedly asks the same questions.
She recently became lost while driving along a familiar neighborhood route to the grocery store.
Cognitive testing yields a Montreal Cognitive Assessment (MoCA) score indicating moderate impairment.
Neurological examination is otherwise normal with intact motor strength, coordination, and cranial nerves.
Non-contrast brain MRI reveals generalized cerebral atrophy with striking disproportionate hippocampal volume loss.
A 32-year-old woman wakes up and notices her face feels strange and heavy on one side.
She has trouble closing her right eye completely and notices that her smile appears noticeably skewed.
She reports a mild, dull ache behind her right ear starting late yesterday evening.
Physical exam reveals complete unilateral paralysis of the entire right side of the face, including the forehead.
Sensation to touch and pinprick over the face remains completely intact and symmetric.
Comprehensive physical and laboratory workup rules out central nervous system lesions and secondary infectious etiologies.
A 28-year-old office worker visits the clinic complaining of an annoying nasal congestion.
He notes that he has been sneezing frequently and feels mildly fatigued since yesterday.
Vital signs show a normal temperature of 37.0°C and clear lung fields on auscultation.
Physical examination reveals mild posterior oropharyngeal erythema without tonsillar exudates or cervical lymphadenopathy.
Nasal mucosa appears boggy and hyperemic with clear watery rhinorrhea.
Symptom pattern and clinical presentation confirm a self-limiting acute viral upper respiratory infection.
A 24-year-old woman visits the urgent care clinic reporting a persistent urge to urinate.
She complains of a sharp, burning discomfort every time she passes urine over the past two days.
She notes that her urine appears slightly cloudy and has a strong, pungent odor.
Physical examination reveals mild suprapubic tenderness without costovertebral angle tenderness or fever.
Urinalysis demonstrates positive nitrite and leukocyte esterase tests with numerous white blood cells.
Urine culture ultimately grows greater than 10,000 colony-forming units of Escherichia coli.
A 30-year-old woman visits the clinic reporting abnormal vaginal discharge.
She notes that the discharge is thick, white, and resembles cottage cheese without a foul odor.
She recently completed a week-long course of broad-spectrum antibiotics for a sinus infection.
Pelvic examination reveals marked vulvar and vaginal mucosal erythema with adherent white plaques.
Wet mount microscopic preparation with potassium hydroxide (KOH) reveals budding yeast cells and pseudohyphae.
Symptoms resolve completely following a single oral dose of fluconazole therapy.
A 25-year-old man visits the urgent care clinic complaining of nausea and watery diarrhea.
He reports experiencing frequent crampy abdominal pain and low-grade fevers since last night.
He mentions several coworkers experienced similar gastrointestinal symptoms after attending a shared catered lunch.
Physical examination reveals mild, diffuse abdominal tenderness without peritoneal signs or organomegaly.
Complete blood count shows a normal white blood cell count with no marked left shift.
Stool multiplex PCR testing detects the presence of Norovirus, confirming the self-limiting diagnosis.
A 6-year-old boy is brought to the pediatrician by his mother due to a rash around his nose and mouth.
She notes the lesions started as small red bumps that quickly ruptured and formed a distinct crust.
The surrounding skin is mildly itchy, and other children at his daycare have reported similar sores.
Physical examination reveals multiple superficial erosions covered by characteristic honey-colored crusts.
Gram stain of the exudate demonstrates clusters of Gram-positive cocci in chains.
Culture of the lesion isolates Staphylococcus aureus, which responds rapidly to topical mupirocin ointment.
A 34-year-old man visits the dermatology clinic complaining of persistent, dry skin lesions.
He notes the patches are mildly itchy and tend to appear over his elbows and knees.
He mentions the condition worsens significantly during winter months and times of emotional stress.
Physical examination reveals well-demarcated erythematous plaques covered by thick, silvery-white scales.
Gentle scraping of the scale reveals tiny pinpoint bleeding spots, known as the Auspitz sign.
Skin biopsy confirms epidermal acanthosis, parakeratosis, and elongated dermal papillae.
A 20-year-old woman visits the clinic complaining of persistent skin itching.
She notes that the itchy patches worsen when she is exposed to wool clothing, harsh soaps, or dry air.
She has a personal history of seasonal allergic rhinitis and childhood asthma.
Physical examination reveals dry, erythematous, lichenified plaques distributed symmetrically in the antecubital and popliteal fossae.
Skin scraping tests are negative for fungal elements, ruling out dermatophyte infections.
Management focuses on aggressive skin barrier moisturization and intermittent topical corticosteroid therapy.
A 29-year-old male athlete visits the clinic complaining of an itchy rash in his groin folds.
He notes the rash has slowly expanded outward, becoming more irritating after intense workout sessions.
Physical examination reveals well-demarcated erythematous plaques with central clearing and raised, scaly borders confined to the inner thighs.
The scrotum is notably spared from the rash involvement.
Potassium hydroxide (KOH) preparation of skin scrapings under microscopy demonstrates branching hyphae.
The condition resolves completely after two weeks of topical terbinafine cream application.
A 40-year-old woman visits the dermatology clinic concerned about persistent facial redness.
She notes that her cheeks and nose flush easily, especially after drinking hot coffee or exercising outdoors.
Physical examination reveals persistent central facial erythema accompanied by prominent telangiectasias.
Examination also shows scattered small inflammatory papules and pustules across the cheeks and chin.
There is a notable absence of comedones, helping to differentiate the condition from acne vulgaris.
Symptoms improve significantly with topical metronidazole gel and strict sun protection.
A 50-year-old woman visits the clinic complaining of joint stiffness and discomfort in both hands.
She reports that the stiffness is most severe in the morning and lasts for more than an hour before improving.
Physical examination reveals symmetric swelling and tenderness of the metacarpophalangeal and proximal interphalangeal joints.
Laboratory evaluation shows an elevated erythrocyte sedimentation rate (ESR) and high C-reactive protein.
Serology tests confirm high titers of rheumatoid factor (RF) and anti-cyclic citrullinated peptide (anti-CCP) antibodies.
Plain radiographs of the hands demonstrate periarticular osteopenia and early marginal joint erosions.
A 52-year-old man wakes up with the sudden onset of pain in his right foot.
He notes that the base of his big toe is extremely tender to even the lightest touch of a bedsheet.
Examination reveals the joint is markedly swollen, erythematous, warm, and shiny.
He admits to attending a celebratory banquet featuring rich red meats and alcohol the prior evening.
Serum laboratory testing reveals a markedly elevated uric acid level.
Polarized light microscopy of synovial fluid aspirated from the joint reveals negatively birefringent needle-shaped crystals.
A 38-year-old man presents to the ER complaining of colicky flank pain.
He paces restlessly around the examination room, unable to find a comfortable resting position.
He reports that the intense pain radiates downward into his groin and testicle.
Physical examination reveals moderate costovertebral angle tenderness without peritoneal signs.
Urinalysis demonstrates microscopic hematuria with no active cellular casts or infection.
Non-contrast helical CT scan of the abdomen and pelvis confirms a 5 mm radiopaque calculus lodged in the distal ureter.
A 70-year-old man is brought to the ER with generalized weakness and lightheadedness.
Family members report he had a severe gastrointestinal bug with persistent vomiting and diarrhea for four days.
Physical exam reveals dry mucous membranes, poor skin turgor, and orthostatic hypotension.
Laboratory evaluation shows a disproportionate rise in blood urea nitrogen relative to serum creatinine, with a BUN-to-creatinine ratio exceeding 20:1.
Urinalysis is completely bland, showing transparent urine with occasional hyaline casts and no active cells.
Fractional excretion of sodium (FeNa) is measured at less than 1%, indicating avid renal tubular sodium retention.
A 6-year-old boy is brought to the pediatrician by his parents due to noticeable puffiness around his eyes.
His parents report that his abdomen has steadily swelled and his shoes feel tight over the past week.
Physical examination reveals generalized pitting edema, particularly prominent in the periorbital and lower extremity regions.
Urinalysis demonstrates massive proteinuria with 4+ protein on dipstick testing and no cellular casts.
Serum chemistry panel reveals severe hypoalbuminemia and hyperlipidemia with normal renal function.
Renal biopsy light microscopy appears completely normal, while electron microscopy shows diffuse effacement of podocyte foot processes.
A 65-year-old man visits the clinic complaining of a progressively weaker urinary stream.
He reports waking up four to five times every night to urinate and experiencing bothersome urinary hesitancy.
He notes a lingering sensation of incomplete bladder emptying after each bathroom visit.
Digital rectal examination reveals a symmetrically enlarged, firm, and smooth prostate gland with no palpable nodules.
Serum prostate-specific antigen (PSA) level is mildly elevated, consistent with age-related prostatic growth.
Urodynamic testing demonstrates bladder outlet obstruction with a reduced peak urinary flow rate.
A 36-year-old woman visits the clinic complaining of persistent fatigue, generalized weakness.
She reports experiencing unusually heavy menstrual periods over the past year along with cravings for ice.
Physical examination reveals notable conjunctival pallor and mild glossitis with a smooth, red tongue.
Complete blood count demonstrates a microcytic, hypochromic anemia with a low hemoglobin level.
Iron panel reveals a low serum iron, low ferritin, and an elevated total iron-binding capacity (TIBC).
Peripheral blood smear confirms the presence of small, pale erythrocytes with occasional pencil cells.
A 42-year-old man visits the clinic reporting persistent loss of interest and profound fatigue lasting over two months.
He mentions difficulty falling asleep at night, poor concentration at work, and a noticeable, unintended weight loss.
He describes feeling worthless and admits to occasional passive thoughts that life is not worth living.
Physical and neurological examinations are entirely unremarkable with normal thyroid function tests.
Standardized psychological screening questionnaires confirm severe depressive symptom severity.
Symptoms meet strict DSM-5 criteria, lasting continuously for greater than two weeks and causing significant functional impairment.
A 28-year-old woman visits the clinic reporting frequent anxiety.
She states she feels perpetually restless, easily fatigued, and unable to quiet her racing thoughts.
She notes physical symptoms including muscle tension, irritability, and frequent tension headaches.
Physical examination and routine laboratory workup rule out organic medical causes such as hyperthyroidism.
Psychological evaluation reveals worries that are difficult to control and span multiple domains of daily life.
Diagnosis is confirmed as symptoms cause persistent distress and functional impairment in her professional and social life.
A 30-year-old man visits the clinic reporting sudden intense fear that peaked within minutes.
He notes these episodes are accompanied by a racing heartbeat, shortness of breath, chest tightness, and a fear of dying.
He states he has started avoiding public spaces and driving out of fear of experiencing another sudden attack.
Medical workup in the ER during a prior episode, including an ECG and cardiac enzymes, ruled out an acute coronary syndrome.
Patient reports recurrent, unexpected panic attacks followed by persistent worry about having future attacks.
Clinical interview confirms the diagnosis and initiates cognitive behavioral therapy alongside selective serotonin reuptake inhibitor treatment.
A 24-year-old woman visits the gynecology clinic complaining of irregular menstrual cycles.
She reports struggling with stubborn acne breakouts and recent difficulty managing her weight.
Physical examination reveals mild hirsutism along the jawline and acanthosis nigricans across the back of her neck.
Laboratory evaluation demonstrates elevated serum free testosterone and an increased luteinizing hormone to follicle-stimulating hormone ratio.
Serum prolactin and thyroid-stimulating hormone levels are within normal limits, ruling out alternative endocrine disorders.
Transvaginal ultrasound demonstrates bilaterally enlarged ovaries containing numerous peripheral antral follicles arranged in a "string of pearls" pattern.
A 41-year-old woman visits the clinic complaining of increasingly heavy menstrual bleeding.
She reports feeling a persistent dull pressure and fullness in her lower pelvic region.
She notes that her periods have become so heavy that she frequently passes large blood clots.
Bimanual pelvic examination reveals an irregularly enlarged, mobile, and non-tender uterus with a firm contour.
Complete blood count confirms a secondary microcytic anemia due to chronic menstrual blood loss.
Pelvic ultrasound identifies multiple well-circumscribed, hypoechoic myometrial masses.
A 26-year-old sexually active woman visits the urgent care clinic complaining of unusual vaginal discharge.
She reports having lower abdominal pain that worsens significantly during sexual intercourse and sudden physical movements.
Vital signs reveal a low-grade fever of 38.1°C and mild tachycardia.
Bimanual pelvic examination demonstrates marked lower abdominal tenderness, purulent cervical discharge, and severe cervical motion tenderness (chandelier sign).
Laboratory tests show an elevated white blood cell count, high ESR, and positive cervical nucleic acid amplification tests for Chlamydia trachomatis.
Pelvic ultrasound reveals fluid-filled, thickened fallopian tubes, confirming upper genital tract infection.
A 31-year-old pregnant woman at 26 weeks gestation visits the clinic for routine prenatal screening.
She reports feeling more fatigued than usual, though she attributes it to the normal progression of pregnancy.
Her past medical history is unremarkable, but she has a strong family history of type 2 diabetes.
A 50-gram oral glucose tolerance challenge test yields an elevated blood glucose reading of 155 mg/dL after one hour.
A subsequent 100-gram three-hour confirmatory oral glucose tolerance test demonstrates two or more elevated blood glucose values.
Diagnosis is established, and dietary counseling paired with home blood glucose monitoring is promptly initiated.
a 68-year-old woman with poorly controlled type 2 diabetes presents with severe suprapubic pain, dysuria, and passage of air bubbles in her urine stream (pneumaturia).
Physical examination reveals marked suprapubic tenderness to palpation without flank or costovertebral angle tenderness.
Urinalysis reveals turbid urine with abundant leukocytes, microhematuria, and positive nitrites.
Plain abdominal radiograph displays a characteristic curvilinear ring of gas within the urinary bladder wall outline.
Non-contrast abdominal CT confirms gas localized entirely within the bladder lumen and muscular wall without free intra-abdominal air.
Urine culture grows gas-producing Klebsiella pneumoniae, which clears following intravenous antibiotic therapy and bladder catheter drainage.
A 2-year-old boy is brought to the ER by his parents late at night due to a harsh coughing.
The parents report that his cough sounds distinctively like a barking seal, accompanied by mild hoarseness.
He has experienced low-grade fever and mild upper respiratory symptoms over the preceding two days.
Physical examination reveals mild inspiratory stridor when he is agitated, but no stridor at rest.
Chest and neck radiography demonstrates a characteristic subglottic tracheal narrowing known as the "steeple sign."
The child responds well to a single dose of oral dexamethasone and cool mist administration.
A 6-month-old infant is brought to the clinic by her parents due to a worsening cough and difficulty feeding.
The parents note she has been breathing noticeably faster and wheezing quietly since yesterday morning.
Physical examination reveals a respiratory rate of 56 breaths per minute with mild subcostal and intercostal retractions.
Auscultation of the chest demonstrates diffuse expiratory wheezes and fine crackles bilaterally.
Nasopharyngeal swab rapid antigen testing returns positive for RSV.
Management focuses on supportive care with nasal suctioning, hydration, and close monitoring of oxygen saturation.
A frantic mother brings her 18-month-old toddler to the ER after a shaking episode at home.
She reports her child's arms and legs stiffened and twitched rhythmically for about two minutes before resolving on their own.
The child was noted to feel very warm prior to the episode and currently has a measured temperature of 39.4°C.
Post-ictal examination reveals a sleepy but easily rousable toddler who quickly returns to baseline mental status.
Neurological examination shows no focal deficits, normal tone, and supple neck with no signs of meningismus.
The child is back to baseline within an hour after a single generalized seizure lasting under 15 minutes during the fever, with no recurrence in 24 hours.
A 45-year-old woman visits the ER complaining of sharp pain in her upper right abdomen.
She states the discomfort started a few hours after eating a heavy, greasy dinner and has steadily worsened.
She reports associated symptoms of nausea, mild anorexia, and a low-grade fever.
Physical examination reveals focal tenderness to palpation in the right upper quadrant.
Inspiration halts abruptly when the examiner presses deeply under the right costal margin, yielding a positive Murphy sign.
Abdominal ultrasound demonstrates gallbladder wall thickening, pericholecystic fluid, and a gallstone lodged in the neck.
A 28-year-old man is brought to the ER by paramedics found unresponsive in a public restroom.
Paramedics report finding empty prescription pill bottles and a hypodermic needle near the patient.
Physical examination reveals profound lethargy, unresponsiveness to verbal stimuli, and a dangerously low respiratory rate of 6 breaths per minute.
Auscultation of the lungs reveals clear breath sounds, and skin is cool and clammy.
Examination of the eyes demonstrates marked pinpoint pupils (miosis) bilaterally.
Immediate administration of intravenous naloxone results in rapid reversal of respiratory depression and prompt awakening.
A 25-year-old woman is rushed to the ER minutes after eating a dessert at a restaurant.
She reports a sudden, overwhelming sensation of warmth, throat tightness, and difficulty swallowing.
Physical examination reveals diffuse, raised erythematous hives across her torso and swelling of her lips and tongue.
Vital signs show a blood pressure of 82/50 mmHg and a rapid heart rate of 125 beats per minute.
Auscultation of the chest demonstrates loud inspiratory stridor and diffuse expiratory wheezing.
Prompt intramuscular injection of epinephrine reverses symptoms, restoring hemodynamic stability and normal airway patency.
A 7-year-old boy is brought to the pediatric clinic by his parents due to intense nocturnal perianal itching and restless sleep over the past week.
Physical examination of the perianal region is unremarkable except for mild skin excoriations and mild erythema secondary to frequent scratching.
Stool routine microscopy for ova and parasites is frequently negative because the adult worms do not routinely release eggs into the feces.
Clear adhesive tape applied to the perianal skin first thing in the morning reveals characteristic asymmetrical, flattened, bean-shaped embryonated eggs under microscopy.
Identification of the parasite confirms infestation by the nematode Enterobius vermicularis.
Complete eradication of symptoms is achieved following a single oral dose of albendazole, repeated in two weeks to prevent reinfection.
A 25-year-old elementary school teacher visits the clinic complaining of redness and irritation in her left eye.
She reports waking up with her eyelids stuck shut by thick, yellowish-green discharge.
She notes a gritty sensation in the eye, though her vision remains clear and unblurred.
Physical examination reveals marked conjunctival injection and hyperemia of the palpebral and bulbar conjunctiva.
There is no corneal staining with fluorescein dye and pupillary reflexes are normal.
Prescribed topical broad-spectrum antibiotic eye drops resolve the purulent discharge within several days.
A 4-year-old girl is brought to the pediatric clinic by her father due to severe right ear pain and irritability.
The father notes she has had a nasal congestion and mild cough for the past four days.
Physical examination reveals a temperature of 38.8°C and a child in moderate distress.
Otoscopic examination of the right ear shows a bright red, bulging tympanic membrane with loss of the normal light reflex.
Pneumatic otoscopy demonstrates markedly reduced mobility of the tympanic membrane due to fluid accumulation.
Symptoms improve dramatically within 48 hours of starting oral antibiotic therapy.
A 23-year-old college student presents to the sexual health clinic noticing several small, flesh-colored bumps in his perianal region that have slowly grown over the past two months.
Physical examination reveals multiple soft, hyperpigmented, cauliflower-like papules clustered around the anal margin without ulceration or inguinal lymphadenopathy.
Vital signs are entirely within normal limits, and systemic physical examination is completely unremarkable.
Application of 5% acetic acid solution (white vinegar test) causes the lesions to turn distinctly white (acetowhitening).
Histopathological biopsy of a lesion demonstrates koilocytosis in the superficial squamous epithelium, acanthosis, and papillary projections.
Polymerase chain reaction (PCR) typing confirms infection with low-risk Human Papillomavirus types 6 and 11, and the lesions resolve following topical podofilox application.
A 26-year-old woman presents to the urgent care clinic with a 2-day history of severe left flank pain.
Physical examination reveals marked left costovertebral angle tenderness on percussion, along with a body temperature of 38.9°C (102°F).
Urinalysis shows turbid urine with positive leukocyte esterase, nitrites, and abundant white blood cell casts.
Renal ultrasound demonstrates a swollen left kidney with parenchymal hypoechogenicity but no urinary tract obstruction.
Urine culture isolates >100,000 CFU/mL of Escherichia coli sensitive to fluoroquinolones and third-generation cephalosporins.
Resolution of flank pain and fever defervescence occur within 48 hours of starting oral ciprofloxacin therapy.
A 22-year-old soccer player visits the orthopedic clinic reporting left knee instability after a sudden pivoting maneuver during a match.
He recalls hearing a distinct popping sound at the moment of injury, followed by rapid joint swelling.
He states that his knee feels loose and frequently "gives out" when he tries to change direction.
Physical examination reveals a large joint effusion and a positive anterior drawer test.
Examination also demonstrates increased anterior tibial translation during the Lachman test with a firm endpoint missing.
Magnetic resonance imaging of the left knee confirms a complete tear of the ACL.
A 35-year-old recreational runner visits the orthopedic clinic complaining of persistent right knee pain and locking.
He notes that his knee occasionally catches and refuses to straighten fully when he stands up from a squatting position.
He recalls twisting his flexed knee while playing basketball a week ago.
Physical examination demonstrates localized tenderness along the joint line and a positive McMurray test reproducing a painful click.
Range of motion is limited by mechanical block during terminal knee extension.
MRI of the right knee confirms a displaced tear involving the posterior horn of the medial meniscus.
A 48-year-old computer programmer visits the clinic complaining of numbness in her right hand.
She notes that the symptoms primarily affect her thumb, index, and middle fingers and often wake her up at night.
She reports that shaking her hand provides temporary relief from the uncomfortable paresthesias.
Physical examination reveals decreased sensation to light touch over the palmar aspect of the first three digits.
Tapping over the volar wrist crease reproduces the tingling sensations, yielding a positive Tinel sign.
Wrist flexion held for 60 seconds reproduces her symptoms, confirming a positive Phalen test.
A 24-year-old woman visits the outpatient clinic complaining of an itchy red rash on her left forearm over the past two weeks.
Physical examination displays an annular erythematous plaque with a raised scaly border and central clearing on the volar left forearm.
Vital signs are entirely within normal limits, and systemic physical examination is unremarkable.
Potassium hydroxide (KOH) preparation of skin scrapings from the active border reveals branching, segmented fungal hyphae.
Fungal culture on Sabouraud dextrose agar yields growth of Trichophyton rubrum.
Rapid resolution of the lesion follows topical application of terbinafine 1% cream, confirming the fungal dermatophyte infection.
A 65-year-old man visits the eye clinic for a routine annual vision check and reports no visual complaints.
He denies any eye pain, redness, or sudden loss of vision, though he notes some difficulty reading small print.
His past medical history is significant for mild essential hypertension managed with medication.
Tonometry measurement reveals elevated intraocular pressures of 26 mmHg in both eyes.
Slit-lamp examination demonstrates open, normal-appearing anterior chamber angles bilaterally.
Fundoscopic examination reveals progressive cupping of the optic discs with an increased cup-to-disc ratio.
A 22-year-old college student visits the student health center complaining of a sore throat.
He reports feeling mildly fatigued with a low-grade fever and mild body aches over the last two days.
He notes that swallowing feels uncomfortable, but he does not experience severe difficulty breathing or drooling.
Physical examination reveals mild diffuse oropharyngeal erythema without tonsillar exudates or palatal petechiae.
Palpation of the neck demonstrates small, mobile, non-tender anterior cervical lymph nodes.
Rapid streptococcal antigen test returns negative, supporting a self-limiting upper respiratory infection.
A 30-year-old woman visits the eye clinic complaining of a painful, tender red bump on her upper eyelid.
She notes the lump developed rapidly over the past 48 hours and feels gritty when she blinks.
Physical examination reveals a localized, erythematous, tender nodule situated at the eyelid margin.
Examination demonstrates a small central yellowish pustule pointing near the base of an eyelash follicle.
Conjunctiva is clear with no widespread discharge or corneal staining.
The lesion resolves completely with warm compresses and topical antibiotic ointment application.
A 29-year-old gardener visits the clinic complaining of an itchy rash on both forearms.
She reports that the rash appeared in linear streaks two days after clearing brush and planting shrubs in her yard.
Physical examination reveals erythematous papules, microvesicles, and linear bullae distributed across exposed skin surfaces.
Scrapings for fungal elements are completely negative, ruling out superficial dermatophyte infection.
Patient history confirms recent exposure to urushiol plant oils while working outdoors.
The acute inflammatory reaction resolves with a tapering course of oral systemic corticosteroids and topical barrier creams.
A 45-year-old runner visits the clinic complaining of sharp heel pain in his right foot.
He notes that the pain is most intense during his very first steps out of bed in the morning.
He mentions that the discomfort improves slightly with walking but worsens after prolonged standing at work.
Physical examination reveals focal tenderness to palpation at the medial calcaneal tuberosity.
Passive dorsiflexion of the toes while palpating the sole reproduces the sharp localized heel pain.
Radiographs show a small calcaneal spur, confirming chronic traction-induced inflammation of the plantar aponeurosis.
A 35-year-old man visits the urgent care clinic complaining of thick nasal discharge.
He reports that his symptoms started as a common cold ten days ago but progressively worsened rather than improving.
He notes a dull ache across his upper teeth and cheekbones accompanied by daytime fatigue.
Physical examination reveals tenderness to percussion over the maxillary sinuses.
Anterior rhinoscopy shows purulent secretions draining from the middle meatus.
Symptoms resolve successfully following a prescribed course of amoxicillin-clavulanate.
A 20-year-old college swimmer visits the clinic complaining of severe pain in his left ear.
He notes that the ear feels clogged and hurts intensely whenever he chews food or pulls on his outer ear.
He spent several hours swimming in outdoor community pools over the weekend.
Physical examination reveals marked tenderness when manipulating the tragus and auricle.
Otoscopic inspection shows marked edema and erythema of the external auditory canal with debris.
Condition resolves completely following administration of topical ciprofloxacin-dexamethasone ear drops.
A 27-year-old woman visits the urgent care clinic complaining of a intensely itchy skin rash.
She notes that individual raised welts appear and disappear across her arms and torso within hours.
She reports no recent respiratory distress, throat swelling, or systemic symptoms.
Physical examination reveals multiple circumscribed, raised erythematous plaques with central pallor scattered across the skin.
Applying firm pressure to the lesions causes temporary blanching of the redness.
Symptoms resolve promptly after administration of oral second-generation antihistamines and identifying the trigger.
A 32-year-old nursing home worker visits the clinic complaining of severe, unyielding nocturnal itching.
She notes that several residents at her facility have reported experiencing similar skin irritation.
Physical examination reveals small erythematous papules and thread-like greyish burrows located in the finger webs and wrist creases.
Microscopic examination of skin scrapings mixed with mineral oil confirms the presence of mites and eggs.
Post-auricular and facial skin regions are completely spared from involvement.
Symptoms resolve following treatment with topical permethrin cream applied from the neck down.
A 62-year-old vegan man visits the clinic complaining of progressive fatigue.
He notes that he has been feeling increasingly clumsy and unsteady while walking over the past few months.
Physical examination reveals conjunctival pallor and loss of vibratory and position sense in the lower extremities.
Complete blood count demonstrates a macrocytic anemia with an elevated mean corpuscular volume (MCV).
Peripheral blood smear shows macro-ovalocytes and hypersegmented neutrophils.
Serum vitamin B12 level is markedly low, and intramuscular supplementation lead to steady clinical improvement.
A 26-year-old dental hygienist presents to the employee health clinic with a 3-day history of a painful swelling on the distal phalanx of her right index finger.
Physical examination reveals an erythematous, edematous fingertip with grouped, painful vesicular and bullous lesions clustered around the nail bed without purulence.
Vital signs are completely normal, though the patient reports mild ipsilateral epitrochlear and axillary lymph node tenderness.
Tzanck smear preparation scraped from the base of a ruptured vesicle reveals multinucleated giant keratinocytes.
Viral culture and PCR testing of the vesicular fluid confirm the presence of Herpes Simplex Virus type 1 (HSV-1).
Complete resolution and drying of the lesions occur within a week following oral acyclovir therapy and protective dressing.
A 19-year-old college student visits the student health center limping on his right foot.
He reports that his ankle rolled inward while stepping off a curb during a jog earlier today.
Physical examination reveals mild swelling and tenderness localized over the lateral aspect of the right ankle.
Palpation along the posterior edge of the medial and lateral malleoli elicits no tenderness.
Patient is able to bear weight for four steps in the clinic, ruling out major bony fracture per Ottawa rules.
Condition improves with rest, ice, compression, elevation, and gentle early mobilization.
A 48-year-old woman visits the clinic reporting dull, steady pain in her upper right abdomen.
She notes episodes of pain typically last between 30 and 90 minutes and frequently occur after eating fatty meals.
She reports no associated fever, chills, jaundice, or persistent vomiting between episodes.
Physical examination reveals a soft abdomen with mild right upper quadrant tenderness and no peritoneal signs.
Laboratory tests including complete blood count, liver function panels, and serum lipase are entirely within normal limits.
Abdominal ultrasound confirms the presence of multiple small gallstones without evidence of gallbladder wall thickening.
A 38-year-old man visits the dermatology clinic complaining of an itchy, flaky scalp.
He notes that yellowish, greasy scales tend to form along his eyebrows, hairline, and sides of his nose.
Physical examination reveals well-demarcated erythematous plaques covered by fine greasy scales distributed in seborrheic zones.
Scrapings for fungal elements are negative, ruling out active dermatophyte infection.
Patient history notes that symptoms tend to worsen during periods of stress and dry winter weather.
The condition responds favorably to treatment with medicated shampoos containing ketoconazole and mild topical antifungals.
A 65-year-old man visits the dermatology clinic concerned about rough, dry spots on his face and scalp.
He notes that these patches feel like sandpaper when he touches them and occasionally become tender.
He has a long-standing history of working outdoors as a construction worker without consistent sun protection.
Physical examination reveals multiple small, scaly, hyperkeratotic papules adherent to sun-exposed skin surfaces.
There is no surrounding induration, ulceration, or deep nodularity on palpation.
Biopsy confirms atypical keratinocyte proliferation confined to the lower epidermis, establishing a precancerous lesion.
a 12-year-old child is brought to the clinic by a parent because of rough bumps on the fingers.
the parent notes the lesions have slowly multiplied over the past few months without causing pain.
physical examination reveals firm, hyperkeratotic papules with a characteristic rough surface on the dorsal hands.
close inspection with magnification reveals tiny black dots representing thrombosed capillary loops.
skin scrapings and fungal cultures are completely negative.
history confirms benign cutaneous infection caused by human papillomavirus (HPV).
A 42-year-old man visits the urgent care clinic complaining of a persistent cough lasting over a week.
He reports coughing up clear to yellowish mucus accompanied by mild substernal chest discomfort when breathing deeply.
He notes a recent antecedent viral upper respiratory infection with nasal congestion and sore throat.
Vital signs reveal a normal temperature of 37.2°C and clear oxygen saturation levels.
Lung auscultation demonstrates scattered rhonchi and coarse breath sounds that clear partially after coughing.
Chest radiography shows no focal infiltrates or consolidation, confirming a self-limiting viral lower respiratory tract inflammation.
A 27-year-old woman visits the clinic complaining of a tingling and burning sensation on her lip.
She notes that a cluster of small, painful fluid-filled blisters has started to form at the vermilion border.
She reports a history of recurrent similar outbreaks triggered by sun exposure and emotional stress.
Physical examination reveals clustered small vesicles on an erythematous base near the right corner of the mouth.
Tzanck smear or viral PCR testing confirms herpes simplex virus type 1 infection.
Lesions crust over and heal completely within a week, aided by topical antiviral therapy.
A 45-year-old man visits the ER complaining of persistent fatigue and night sweats.
He notes experiencing intermittent fevers, chills, and a vague aching in his joints over the past three weeks.
Physical examination reveals a new blowing systolic murmur heard best at the left lower sternal border.
Examination demonstrates small, non-tender hemorrhagic macules on his palms known as Janeway lesions.
Laboratory tests show an elevated erythrocyte sedimentation rate and continuous bacteremia on blood cultures.
Transthoracic echocardiography identifies mobile vegetation attached to the tricuspid valve leaflet.
A 70-year-old man visits the cardiology clinic reporting progressive shortness of breath during light physical exertion.
He mentions experiencing a brief episode of lightheadedness while walking up a flight of stairs last week.
Physical examination reveals a harsh, crescendo-decrescendo systolic ejection murmur heard best at the right second intercostal space.
Auscultation demonstrates radiation of the cardiac murmur upward along the carotid arteries.
Electrocardiogram shows signs of left ventricular hypertrophy with strain patterns.
Transthoracic echocardiography confirms severe valve narrowing with a reduced aortic valve area and high transvalvular gradient.
A 31-year-old man visits the ER reporting the sudden onset of sharp chest pain.
He notices that the pain worsens significantly when he lies flat on his back and improves when he leans forward.
He reports recovering from a viral upper respiratory illness a week prior to symptom onset.
Physical examination reveals a high-pitched, scratchy friction rub heard best along the left sternal border at end-expiration.
12-lead ECG demonstrates widespread diffuse concave ST-segment elevations and PR-segment depressions.
Echocardiography shows a small pericardial effusion without signs of right atrial or ventricular collapse.
A 19-year-old man visits the clinic for a routine sports physical examination and is found to have elevated blood pressure.
He reports occasional headaches and unusual fatigue in his legs when running long distances.
Physical examination reveals bounding pulses in the upper extremities with noticeably delayed and weak femoral pulses.
Auscultation demonstrates a systolic ejection murmur heard best over the left interscapular region of the back.
Chest X-ray reveals characteristic inferior rib notching caused by dilated collateral intercostal arteries.
Computed tomography angiography of the chest confirms a localized narrowing of the aorta distal to the left subclavian artery.
A 52-year-old woman visits the ER complaining of sudden-onset shortness of breath and chest pain.
She notes that her symptoms began shortly after completing a grueling 12-hour cross-country airplane flight.
Vital signs reveal tachypnea, a heart rate of 115 bpm, and a normal blood pressure.
Physical examination of the lower extremities shows mild swelling and tenderness in her left calf.
Arterial blood gas analysis demonstrates acute respiratory alkalosis with hypoxemia.
CT pulmonary angiography confirms a filling defect occluding a segmental branch of the right pulmonary artery.
A 10-year-old child is brought to the pediatric clinic by parents reporting chronic productive coughing.
The parents note that the child has a history of frequent foul-smelling, greasy stools and recurrent pulmonary infections.
Physical examination reveals a thin child with increased anteroposterior chest diameter and clubbing of the fingers.
Sweat chloride testing demonstrates markedly elevated chloride concentrations well above the diagnostic threshold.
Genetic testing confirms homozygous mutations in the CFTR gene.
Sputum cultures isolate chronic colonization with Pseudomonas aeruginosa.
A 25-year-old man is rushed to the ER following a high-speed motor vehicle collision with severe respiratory distress.
Vital signs reveal profound hypotension, tracheal deviation away from the affected side, and absent breath sounds unilaterally.
Physical examination demonstrates hyperresonance to percussion and distended neck veins.
Emergency needle decompression is performed immediately in the second intercostal space with a rush of air.
Chest tube insertion confirms re-expansion of the collapsed lung.
Chest radiography shows complete collapse of the right lung with mediastinal shift.
A 28-year-old man visits the ER reporting acute hemoptysis and progressive shortness of breath over the past week.
He notes that his urine has recently turned a dark, tea-colored shade accompanied by decreased daily output.
Laboratory evaluation reveals rapidly worsening renal function with elevated serum creatinine and active urinary sediment.
Serum testing demonstrates high titers of circulating anti-glomerular basement membrane (anti-GBM) antibodies.
Chest X-ray reveals bilateral patchy alveolar infiltrates due to pulmonary hemorrhage.
Renal biopsy immunofluorescence shows linear IgG deposition along the glomerular basement membranes.
A 22-year-old woman visits the clinic complaining of chronic right lower quadrant abdominal pain.
She reports experiencing persistent non-bloody diarrhea, low-grade fevers, significant unintended weight loss, and painful aphthous mouth ulcers.
Physical examination reveals a tender, palpable mass in the right lower abdominal quadrant and a perianal skin tag.
Colonoscopy demonstrates discontinuous segments of inflamed mucosa with deep ulcerations separated by normal areas (skip lesions).
Biopsy confirms transmural inflammation with non-caseating granulomas.
CT enterography shows wall thickening and stricturing involving the terminal ileum.
A 30-year-old man visits the clinic reporting recurrent episodes of bloody diarrhea and crampy lower abdominal pain.
He notes a frequent, urgent need to defecate accompanied by a sensation of incomplete evacuation (tenesmus).
Laboratory workup reveals microcytic anemia and an elevated erythrocyte sedimentation rate.
Flexible sigmoidoscopy demonstrates continuous, friable mucosal erythema extending proximally from the rectum without skip areas.
Histological examination reveals crypt abscesses and architectural distortion limited to the mucosa and submucosa.
Barium enema shows loss of normal haustral markings, producing a smooth "lead pipe" appearance of the colon.
A 35-year-old woman visits the clinic complaining of chronic bloating, gas, and recurrent foul-smelling diarrhea.
She notes feeling chronically fatigued and mentions an itchy, blistering rash distributed symmetrically on her elbows and knees.
Blood tests reveal an iron-deficiency anemia refractory to oral iron supplementation.
Serological evaluation shows strongly positive anti-tissue transglutaminase (anti-tTG) IgA antibodies.
Upper endoscopy with duodenal biopsy demonstrates blunting of the villi and crypt hyperplasia.
Symptoms and serology normalize completely following strict elimination of dietary gluten.
A 38-year-old woman visits the clinic complaining of unintentional weight loss.
She reports feeling nervous, irritable, and noticing a fine tremor in her hands when writing.
Physical examination reveals a symmetrically enlarged, soft goiter with a palpable thrill and audible bruit.
Examination also shows lid lag and bilateral exophthalmos with mild periorbital edema.
Laboratory tests demonstrate suppressed serum TSH levels with markedly elevated free T3 and free T4.
Serology confirms the presence of circulating thyroid-stimulating immunoglobulin (TSI) antibodies.
A 42-year-old woman visits the endocrinology clinic complaining of progressive weight gain.
She notes developing central obesity, a prominent fat pad on the back of her neck, and purple stretch marks on her abdomen.
Physical examination reveals a rounded "moon facies," facial plethora, and proximal muscle weakness in the legs.
Laboratory evaluation shows persistent hyperglycemia and an elevated 24-hour urinary free cortisol excretion.
Overnight low-dose dexamethasone suppression test fails to suppress serum cortisol levels.
Plasma ACTH levels and pituitary MRI identify a microadenoma driving excessive cortisol production.
A 45-year-old man visits the clinic complaining of profound fatigue, weakness.
He notes experiencing chronic dizziness when standing up, along with salt cravings and nausea.
Physical examination reveals hyperpigmentation of the palmar creases, gum margins, and recent scars.
Laboratory evaluation demonstrates hyponatremia, hyperkalemia, and a low baseline morning serum cortisol.
Cosyntropin stimulation test confirms primary adrenal insufficiency with a blunted cortisol response.
Serology confirms autoimmune adrenalitis through positive anti-21-hydroxylase antibodies.
A 55-year-old woman visits the clinic reporting recurrent kidney stones.
She mentions experiencing vague bone aches and constipation.
Routine metabolic panel reveals persistent hypercalcemia paired with an elevated serum parathyroid hormone level.
24-hour urine collection demonstrates hypercalciuria and elevated urinary cyclic AMP.
Serum phosphate levels are concurrently low due to renal tubular wasting.
Technetium-99m sestamibi scintigraphy localizes a hyperfunctioning parathyroid adenoma.
A 65-year-old man visits the neurology clinic complaining of a tremor in his right hand.
He notes that his handwriting has become progressively smaller and cramped over the past year.
Physical examination reveals a slow shuffling gait with decreased arm swing and masked facial expression.
Examination demonstrates cogwheel rigidity and bradykinesia during passive limb movement.
Neurological evaluation confirms the absence of cerebellar signs or early dementia.
Patient experiences significant symptomatic improvement following the initiation of carbidopa-levodopa therapy.
A 30-year-old man visits the neurology clinic reporting repeated attacks of severe pain around his right eye.
He states the attacks occur daily at the exact same time, lasting about 45 minutes, and awaken him from sleep.
Physical examination during an attack reveals ipsilateral conjunctival injection, lacrimation, nasal congestion, and miosis.
Patient is noted to pace restlessly during episodes, unlike patients with migraines who prefer resting in a dark room.
Neurological examination between headache bouts is entirely normal.
High-flow oxygen inhalation and subcutaneous sumatriptan abort acute attacks successfully.
A 48-year-old man is brought to the ER with acute confusion.
Family members report he has eaten very little solid food over the past several weeks, relying mostly on alcohol.
Physical examination reveals bilateral lateral rectus palsies, horizontal nystagmus, and severe ataxia.
Neurological evaluation reveals global confusion and impaired short-term memory.
Immediate administration of intravenous thiamine prevents progression to Korsakoff syndrome.
Brain MRI shows symmetrical hyperintensities in the medial thalami and periaqueductal gray matter.
A 34-year-old traveler visits the ER complaining of high-grade fever, shaking chills.
He reports returning from a two-week trip to sub-Saharan Africa a week ago.
Physical examination reveals splenomegaly and mild jaundice with clear lungs.
Complete blood count demonstrates hemolytic anemia, thrombocytopenia, and elevated total bilirubin.
Thick and thin peripheral blood smears examined under microscopy reveal ring-form trophozoites inside erythrocytes.
Rapid diagnostic antigen test confirms infection with Plasmodium falciparum.
A 40-year-old hiker visits the clinic complaining of fatigue, generalized muscle aches.
He reports spending a weekend camping in a wooded area in the northeastern United States three weeks ago.
Physical examination reveals a large, expanding annular erythematous patch with central clearing on his thigh (erythema migrans).
Vital signs show a normal temperature and no signs of acute arthritic joint swelling.
Two-tier serological testing using ELISA followed by Western blot confirms IgG and IgM antibodies to Borrelia burgdorferi.
Symptoms resolve completely following a standard course of oral doxycycline therapy.
A 50-year-old immigrant visits the clinic complaining of a persistent cough lasting over two months.
He reports experiencing drenching night sweats, afternoon low-grade fevers, and noticeable unintentional weight loss.
Physical examination reveals decreased breath sounds and post-tussive apical rales over the right upper lung field.
Chest radiography demonstrates cavitary lesions and patchy infiltrates localized to the right upper lobe.
Acid-fast bacilli (AFB) smear of sputum yields positive results.
Sputum culture grows slow-growing, cord-forming acid-fast bacilli after several weeks, and a nucleic acid amplification test is positive.
A 32-year-old man visits the clinic complaining of persistent fatigue, chronic diarrhea.
He reports a significant, unintended weight loss of 10 kg over the past three months.
Physical examination reveals painless generalized lymphadenopathy and thick white plaques on the lateral tongue and palate.
Laboratory workup reveals a profoundly low CD4+ T-lymphocyte count falling below 200 cells/microliter.
Serum HIV-1/2 antigen/antibody combination immunoassay returns positive, confirmed by viral load testing.
Chest X-ray demonstrates diffuse interstitial infiltrates indicative of concurrent Pneumocystis jirovecii pneumonia.
A 28-year-old man visits the sexual health clinic complaining of non-itchy skin rash.
He notes that the rash involves his palms and soles, accompanied by generalized lymphadenopathy and malaise.
He reports having a painless genital ulcer several weeks prior that spontaneously healed without treatment.
Physical examination reveals reddish-brown maculopapular lesions across the trunk, palms, and soles.
Venereal Disease Research Laboratory (VDRL) screening test returns reactive with a high titer.
Confirmatory FTA-ABS testing is reactive, and the patient also has painless, moist, wart-like plaques in the perianal region.
A 29-year-old traveler returning from Southeast Asia visits the ER with high-grade fever and headache.
He describes experiencing intense retro-orbital pain and severe myalgias.
Physical examination reveals a flushed face and a transient erythematous maculopapular rash across his trunk.
Complete blood count demonstrates marked leukopenia and severe thrombocytopenia.
Tourniquet test yields petechiae formation, indicating fragile capillary walls.
Serum IgM capture ELISA confirms acute dengue virus infection.
A 50-year-old man with poorly controlled diabetes visits the ER complaining of rapidly worsening pain in his left leg.
He notes that the pain is disproportionately severe compared to the mild skin redness observed initially.
Physical examination reveals tense edema, dusky skin discoloration, and crepitus upon palpation of the calf.
Vital signs demonstrate high fever, tachycardia, and early septic shock parameters.
Laboratory tests show profound leukocytosis, elevated serum lactate, and severe hyponatremia.
Emergency surgical exploration reveals necrotic fascia with dishwater-gray discharge, confirming surgical debridement necessity.
A 24-year-old woman visits the dermatology clinic concerned about hair loss on her scalp.
She notes finding clumps of hair on her pillow and discovering smooth, completely bald patches over the past two weeks.
Physical examination reveals well-demarcated, completely smooth, non-scarring circular patches of hair loss.
Examination of the patch margins reveals short, tapered hairs that are narrower near the skin surface ("exclamation point hairs").
Scalp skin appears normal with no scaling, erythema, or follicular plugging.
Biopsy confirms a peribulbar lymphocytic infiltrate attacking anagen hair follicles in an autoimmune fashion.
A 52-year-old man visits the dermatology clinic for a routine skin check and points out a dark mole on his back.
He notes that the mole has recently changed in size, shape, and color, and occasionally bleeds with friction.
Physical examination reveals an asymmetric pigmented lesion with irregular borders, variegated color shades, and a diameter exceeding 6 mm.
Dermoscopic evaluation shows an atypical pigment network, blue-white veil, and irregular streaks.
Palpation reveals no palpable regional lymphadenopathy in the axillary basins.
Excisional biopsy shows atypical melanocytes invading the dermis, with a Breslow thickness of 1.5 mm.
A 22-year-old college student presents bilateral eye itching, watering over the past week.
Visual acuity is 20/20 bilaterally, pupils are equal and reactive, and corneas remain clear without staining defects.
Physical examination reveals bilateral chemosis, eyelid edema, and a characteristic "cobblestone" papillary reaction on the tarsal conjunctiva.
Conjunctival scraping reveals a prominent abundance of eosinophils under microscopic examination.
Skin prick testing confirms strong hypersensitivity to local airborne grass and tree pollens.
Rapid relief of ocular pruritus and inflammation is achieved with topical dual-action antihistamine/mast cell stabilizer eye drops (olopatadine).
A 28-year-old woman visits the rheumatology clinic complaining of persistent fatigue and painful joints swelling.
She notes developing a red, flat facial rash across her cheeks and bridge of the nose that worsens after sun exposure.
Physical examination reveals a classic malar rash sparing the nasolabial folds and non-erosive arthritis in the fingers.
Laboratory workup demonstrates leukopenia, proteinuria, and an elevated erythrocyte sedimentation rate.
Serology reveals strongly positive antinuclear antibodies (ANA) and elevated anti-double-stranded DNA antibodies.
Complement levels (C3 and C4) are markedly depressed, reflecting active immune complex consumption.
A 26-year-old man visits the clinic complaining of chronic lower back pain over the past three months.
Physical examination reveals decreased lumbar spine range of motion and diminished chest expansion during inspiration.
He notes that the back pain improves with physical exercise and worsens significantly with prolonged periods of rest.
Modified Schober test demonstrates significantly restricted forward flexion of the lumbar spine.
Laboratory tests show a normal rheumatoid factor and elevated inflammatory markers.
Pelvic radiography reveals bilateral sacroiliitis and syndesmophyte formation, producing a characteristic "bamboo spine."
A 72-year-old woman visits the clinic complaining of aching in her shoulders and hips.
She reports having morning stiffness, so severe that she struggles to lift her arms to comb her hair or rise from a chair.
Physical examination reveals normal muscle strength despite the severe pain with active and passive range of motion.
Laboratory evaluation demonstrates a markedly elevated erythrocyte sedimentation rate (ESR) and high C-reactive protein.
Serum creatine kinase levels are completely normal, ruling out primary inflammatory myopathies.
Symptoms resolve dramatically within 48 hours of initiating low-dose oral corticosteroid therapy.
A 25-year-old man visits the urgent care clinic complaining of painful swelling in his right knee and left ankle.
He reports recovering from a gastrointestinal bacterial illness following a camping trip three weeks ago.
He notes experiencing a burning sensation during urination and redness in both eyes over the past week.
Physical examination reveals asymmetric oligoarthritis of the lower extremities, conjunctivitis, and painless oral ulcers.
Urethral swab confirms the antecedent enteric infection without active gonococcal urethritis.
Genetic testing demonstrates strong positivity for the HLA-B27 allele.
A 68-year-old man in the ICU is noted to have a rapidly rising serum creatinine level over 48 hours.
He reports decreased urine output despite adequate fluid resuscitation following cardiac bypass surgery.
Urinalysis demonstrates muddy brown granular casts and epithelial cell casts under microscopy.
Fractional excretion of sodium (FeNa) is measured at greater than 2%, indicating ATN.
Renal ultrasound reveals normal kidney size without hydronephrosis or urinary obstruction.
Laboratory workup rules out prerenal azotemia and obstructive postrenal etiologies.
A 40-year-old man visits the clinic reporting episodes of dull flank pain and visible blood in his urine.
His past medical history is significant for newly diagnosed essential hypertension and a strong family history of kidney failure.
Physical examination reveals bilateral, ballotable, irregularly enlarged abdominal masses corresponding to the kidneys.
Urinalysis confirms persistent microscopic hematuria and mild proteinuria.
Renal function panel shows a slowly rising serum creatinine concentration.
Abdominal CT scan demonstrates countless fluid-filled cysts replacing both renal parenchyma alongside hepatic cysts.
A 30-year-old woman visits her primary care doctor reporting recurrent excessive flatulence, and watery diarrhea that occur 30 to 60 minutes after eating.
Physical examination reveals mild, diffuse abdominal distension and hyperactive bowel sounds, with no focal tenderness, guarding, or masses.
Complete blood count, serum chemistry, and stool analysis for occult blood and ova/parasites are entirely normal.
Hydrogen breath test following an oral lactose load demonstrates a significant rise in breath hydrogen concentration (>20 ppm above baseline).
Stool acidity testing reveals a low pH secondary to unabsorbed lactose fermentation by colonic bacteria.
Complete disappearance of gastrointestinal symptoms follows the avoidance of lactose-containing foods and supplementation with lactase enzyme tablets.
A 60-year-old man visits the clinic reporting painless gross hematuria.
He notes an unintentional weight loss of 8 kg and persistent low-grade fevers over the past three months.
Physical examination reveals a palpable right upper quadrant abdominal mass and newly developed right-sided varicocele.
Complete blood count demonstrates secondary erythrocytosis due to paraneoplastic erythropoietin production.
Urinalysis confirms gross hematuria without active cellular casts.
Contrast-enhanced CT scan of the abdomen identifies a solid enhancing mass arising from the right renal cortex.
A 16-year-old adolescent is brought urgently to the ER with the sudden onset of severe right testicular pain.
He reports that the pain woke him from sleep and is accompanied by nausea and vomiting.
Physical examination reveals a high-riding, extremely tender right testicle oriented horizontally in the hemiscrotum.
Elevation of the scrotum fails to relieve the pain, resulting in a negative Prehn sign.
Cremasteric reflex is completely absent on the affected right side.
Color Doppler ultrasound demonstrates an absence of blood flow within the right testicular parenchyma.
a 12-year-old child is brought to the ER reporting sudden, severe pain in both arms and legs.
the parent notes the child experienced a recent viral upper respiratory infection prior to the pain crisis.
physical examination reveals mild scleral icterus and tenderness over the long bones without localized swelling.
complete blood count demonstrates chronic normocytic hemolytic anemia with elevated reticulocyte count.
peripheral blood smear shows characteristic sickle-shaped erythrocytes and Howell-Jolly bodies.
hemoglobin electrophoresis confirms homozygosity for hemoglobin S (HbSS).
A 60-year-old man visits the clinic for a routine annual exam and is found to have asymptomatic lymphocytosis.
Laboratory workup reveals a persistent white blood cell count exceeding 50,000/microliter dominated by mature lymphocytes.
Physical examination demonstrates painless, symmetric cervical and axillary lymphadenopathy alongside mild splenomegaly.
Peripheral blood smear shows numerous small, mature-appearing lymphocytes alongside characteristic "smudge cells."
Flow cytometry confirms a monoclonal B-cell population expressing CD5, CD19, CD20, and CD23 markers.
Bone marrow biopsy reveals diffuse infiltration by small, well-differentiated lymphocytes.
A 24-year-old man visits the clinic complaining of painless swelling in his left side of the neck.
He reports experiencing drenching night sweats, persistent fatigue, and unexplained weight loss over two months.
He notes that lymph node pain flares up predictably after drinking small amounts of alcoholic beverages.
Physical examination reveals firm, rubbery, non-tender cervical and supraclavicular lymphadenopathy.
Chest X-ray demonstrates a prominent anterior mediastinal mass widening the superior mediastinum.
Excisional lymph node biopsy confirms the presence of classic multinucleated Reed-Sternberg cells expressing CD15 and CD30.
A 28-year-old woman visits the clinic reporting easy bruising and scattered pinpoint red spots on her legs.
She notes episodes of spontaneous nosebleeds and heavy menstrual bleeding over the past week.
Physical examination reveals numerous petechiae and purpura on the lower extremities without hepatosplenomegaly.
Complete blood count demonstrates isolated thrombocytopenia with a platelet count of 22,000/microliter and normal hemoglobin.
Peripheral blood smear confirms low platelet numbers with remaining platelets appearing large and normal in morphology.
Bone marrow aspiration shows normal to increased numbers of megakaryocytes, ruling out central bone marrow failure.
A 25-year-old man is brought to the clinic by his family due to bizarre behavioral changes over six months.
Family members report he expresses beliefs that neighbors are monitoring his thoughts through television broadcasts.
He frequently responds to internal auditory stimuli, muttering to voices that no other person can hear.
Mental status examination reveals disorganized speech, flat affect, and paranoid delusions.
Neurological and laboratory evaluations rule out substance-induced psychosis or underlying medical disorders.
Symptoms cause profound functional decline in occupational and social domains, meeting strict DSM-5 criteria.
A 32-year-old woman is brought to the ER by her spouse due to erratic behavior and extreme hyperactivity.
The spouse reports she has gone without sleep for four consecutive days while impulsively starting multiple grandiose business projects.
Mental status examination reveals pressured speech, flight of ideas, distractibility, and reckless financial spending.
History confirms a prior depressive episode lasting several weeks occurring a year ago.
Toxicology screen is completely negative for illicit drug use or stimulant intoxication.
Presentation meets diagnostic criteria for a manic episode, establishing a definitive diagnosis of the disorder.
A 26-year-old man visits the psychiatric clinic complaining of persistent, distressing thoughts that his hands are contaminated.
He reports spending hours every day washing his hands repeatedly until they bleed, driven by a need to relieve intense anxiety.
He recognizes that his fears are excessive and unreasonable, but feels powerless to stop the ritualistic behaviors.
Mental status examination reveals intact cognitive function and prominent checking and washing compulsions.
Psychological evaluation rules out primary depressive disorders or psychotic spectrum illnesses.
Symptoms consume significant time daily, causing marked distress and impairment in daily functioning.
A 34-year-old military combat veteran visits the clinic complaining of severe anxiety and intrusive nightmares.
He reports vivid flashbacks where he feels as though he is back in combat when hearing sudden loud noises.
He actively avoids driving down certain streets and distances himself from social gatherings.
Mental status examination reveals hypervigilance, an exaggerated startle response, and emotional numbing.
Symptoms have persisted continuously for more than three months following exposure to severe trauma.
Presentation causes significant distress and impairs occupational and interpersonal functioning.
A 17-year-old female adolescent is brought to the clinic by her parents due to severe weight loss.
She expresses an intense, overriding fear of gaining weight despite being visibly emaciated.
Physical examination reveals a body mass index of 15 kg/m2, dry skin, lanugo hair, and resting bradycardia.
Laboratory evaluation demonstrates normocytic anemia, electrolyte disturbances, and secondary amenorrhea.
Mental status examination reveals distorted body image where she perceives herself as overweight.
Presentation meets strict DSM-5 criteria for the disorder.
A 32-year-old pregnant woman at 34 weeks gestation visits the clinic reporting a persistent frontal headache.
She notes experiencing sudden swelling in her face and hands accompanied by blurry vision and spots in her visual field.
Vital signs reveal a blood pressure of 162/105 mmHg measured on two occasions four hours apart.
Urine dipstick testing demonstrates 3+ proteinuria exceeding 300 mg in a 24-hour collection.
Laboratory workup shows normal liver enzymes and normal platelet count.
Repeat readings at 34 weeks stay above 160/110 mmHg with a urine protein-to-creatinine ratio above 0.3, prompting admission for delivery planning.
A 28-year-old woman visits the ER complaining of sudden-onset sharp right lower quadrant abdominal pain.
She reports her last menstrual period was six weeks ago.
Physical examination reveals localized right adnexal tenderness and mild pelvic guarding without rebound.
Pregnancy test was positive, quantitative serum beta-hCG testing demonstrates elevated levels that fail to double appropriately over 48 hours.
Transvaginal ultrasound reveals an empty uterine cavity with an extrauterine mass in the right fallopian tube.
Patient is hemodynamically stable, allowing for successful medical management with systemic methotrexate injection.
A 29-year-old woman visits the gynecology clinic complaining of severe menstrual cramps.
She reports experiencing deep pain during sexual intercourse and chronic lower pelvic aching throughout the month.
Bimanual pelvic examination reveals a fixed, retroverted uterus and tender nodularity along the uterosacral ligaments.
Transvaginal ultrasound identifies a cystic adnexal mass with homogeneous low-level internal echoes consistent with an endometrioma.
Laboratory and routine infectious workup are completely negative for pelvic inflammatory disease.
Diagnostic laparoscopy confirms scattered bluish-black "powder-burn" peritoneal lesions across the pelvic cul-de-sac.
A 34-year-old pregnant woman at 32 weeks gestation visits the ER reporting sudden, severe abdominal pain and vaginal bleeding.
She notes that her uterus feels hard, tense, and constantly contracted between pain waves.
Vital signs reveal maternal tachycardia and mild hypotension corresponding to blood loss.
Fetal monitoring demonstrates non-reassuring fetal heart rate tracing with persistent late decelerations.
Transabdominal ultrasound reveals a retroplacental hematoma separating the placenta from the uterine wall.
Emergency Cesarean delivery is performed due to acute fetal distress and maternal instability.
A 4-week-old male infant is brought to the pediatrician by his mother due to frequent vomiting after feeding.
The mother reports that the infant appears hungry and immediately demands to feed again after vomiting.
Physical examination reveals a small, mobile, olive-shaped mass palpable in the right upper abdominal quadrant.
Metabolic panel demonstrates hypochloremic, hypokalemic metabolic alkalosis due to chronic acid loss.
Abdominal ultrasound demonstrates thickening of the pyloric muscle and elongation of the pyloric channel.
Infant undergoes successful pyloromyotomy surgery following preoperative electrolyte correction.
A 7-month-old infant is brought to the ER by parents due to episodic crying and pulling legs toward the chest.
Parents note that the infant appears healthy and playful between painful crying spells lasting several minutes.
Physical examination reveals a sausage-shaped mass palpable in the right upper abdomen.
Diaper inspection reveals dark red, mucus-containing stool often described as "currant jelly."
Abdominal ultrasound demonstrates a classic "target sign" or "donut sign" representing bowel telescoping.
Hydrostatic enema reduction successfully resolves the invagination without requiring surgery.
A 55-year-old man visits the ER complaining of diffuse crampy abdominal pain, nausea, and vomiting.
He reports being completely unable to pass gas or stool over the past 24 hours.
His past medical history is significant for an open appendectomy performed ten years ago.
Physical examination reveals a distended, tympanic abdomen with high-pitched "tinkling" bowel sounds on auscultation.
Complete blood count shows hemoconcentration and electrolyte shifts consistent with third-space fluid losses.
Erect abdominal X-ray demonstrates dilated loops of small bowel with multiple air-fluid levels arranged in a ladder pattern.
A 62-year-old man visits the ER complaining of a firm bulge in his right groin.
He reports that the bulge has been present for years but recently became firm, tender, and intensely painful.
Physical examination reveals an erythematous, tender, non-reducible mass in the right groin extending into the scrotum.
Vital signs show a low-grade fever, tachycardia, and localized skin changes over the hernia sac.
Laboratory tests reveal leukocytosis with a left shift, raising concern for bowel ischemia.
Emergency surgical exploration confirms an incarcerated loop of small bowel requiring resection.
A 21-year-old man is brought to the ER following a bicycle crash involving direct impact to his upper abdomen.
Vital signs demonstrate hemodynamic instability with marked tachycardia and low blood pressure.
He reports severe left upper quadrant abdominal pain radiating upward to his left shoulder.
